pages.text: Rugby in Argentina began long ago. In the middle of the nineteenth century, immigrants brought sports to the country. The very first rugby match was played in the year eighteen seventy-three in Buenos Aires. Later, in nineteen ten, the Argentina national team played its first international match against a visiting team.

evidence.articleCaption: The first Argentina national team ever before playing the British Lions at Sociedad Sportiva Argentina, 12 June 1910

pages.text: During a famous tour of South Africa in nineteen sixty-five, the Argentine team earned the special nickname Los Pumas. This name became a proud identity mark for the country and remains used to this very day. The team also won several early South American tournaments during those decades.

pages.text: In nineteen eighty, important teams toured South America. This allowed Los Pumas to face major rugby nations from around the world. Through the nineteen seventies and nineteen eighties, the team improved greatly with help from star player Hugo Porta, who showed world-class skills on the field.

pages.text: Argentina has played in every single Rugby World Cup since the very first tournament in nineteen eighty-seven. Their best performance in the competition happened in two thousand seven, when they achieved an amazing third place finish after defeating strong opponents during the tournament matches.

pages.text: A major breakthrough came in twenty twelve when Argentina finally joined The Rugby Championship. In this annual competition, they play against powerhouse teams like New Zealand, Australia, and South Africa. This step proved their high status in international rugby union sports.

Rugby union was introduced to Argentina by immigrants during the middle of the nineteenth century, leading to the first recorded match in Buenos Aires in eighteen seventy-three. Decades later, on June twelfth, nineteen ten, the River Plate Rugby Football Union played its first international game against a touring team managed by Oxford University.

pages.text: A defining moment for the sport in Argentina occurred in nineteen sixty-five during a tour of South Africa. The national team earned the famous nickname Los Pumas during these matches, establishing an identity that persists today. Throughout the nineteen fifties and sixties, Argentina also dominated several South American regional tournaments.

pages.text: During the nineteen seventies, the team's steady rise toward top-tier status was heavily influenced by fly-half Hugo Porta, widely regarded as their first truly world-class player. By the nineteen eighties, regular tours allowed the Pumas to test themselves against major international sides from England, France, New Zealand, and Australia.

The pivotal juncture arrived in nineteen sixty-five during a tour of South Africa, where the national squad acquired the enduring moniker Los Pumas, cementing a permanent identity for Argentine rugby on the international stage.
